headline.en: A barbershop chord rings when every voice is tuned to the others, so closely it hums. Here, one note is yours.

detail.en: Four straight voices, tuned
The top note, mi, is yours
A ringing third sits 14 cents under the piano's

text.en: Listen to each chord, as often as you like. Headphones on: through a speaker the mic hears the chord too.

why.en: B's third is 14 cents lower than the piano's: the beating stops and the chord hums.
A has the piano's third: a fast shimmer against the others. B rings.
A's third sits 14 cents low and rings. B is the piano's.

text.en: Try it: hold mi with the three voices, straight, and let it settle where the chord hums. This one's practice. Headphones on: through a speaker the mic hears the chord too.
Now hold mi for four beats, straight, until it rings. Straight, not squeezed: medium-soft. Headphones on: through a speaker the mic hears the chord too.

measures.en: Your stars are for how close your held mi came to ringing: within 6 cents of pure. This first lesson gives a fair try two stars; three need the low third. Barbershop harmony grew from Black American quartet singing of the late 1800s. In unit 4, two of these voices are you.

headline.en: A chord rings on straight tones: no wave. Straight, not squeezed: medium-soft. If your throat tightens, let a little wave back in.

detail.en: One steady line, no wave
Light and medium-soft
A wave blurs the ring

text.en: Hold mi straight over the three voices, then so's place in the chord, a note at a time. Headphones on: through a speaker the mic hears the chord too.

measures.en: Your stars are for how straight your held notes stayed. Was it light, not squeezed?

text.en: Now record your note over the chord twice: once on "oo", once on "ah". Play both back. Headphones on: through a speaker the mic hears the chord too.

questions.en: Which vowel rang more for you, "oo" or "ah"?
Did your throat stay easy on both?

headline.en: One voice out of tune makes the whole chord beat. Find it.

detail.en: Low to high
By about a fifth of a semitone
Which voice is it in?

text.en: Each chord has one voice 20 cents out. Which one? Headphones on: through a speaker the mic hears the chord too.

why.en: The top voice, the tenor, was 20 cents sharp.
The bass, the lowest, was 20 cents flat.
The lead, the octave above the bass, was 20 cents sharp.
The baritone, on so, was 20 cents flat.
B has a voice out: it shimmers. A rings.
A has the piano's third. B rings.

measures.en: Your stars are for the voices you picked out, first time.

headline.en: One chord, three seats: the root, the fifth or the third. Lock each one.

detail.en: Do, the floor of the chord
So, where the piano puts it
Mi, 14 cents low

text.en: The fifth, the easy seat: hold so while the others sing theirs. Straight, not squeezed: medium-soft. Headphones on: through a speaker the mic hears the chord too.
The root: hold do while the others sing around you. Straight, not squeezed: medium-soft. Headphones on: through a speaker the mic hears the chord too.
And the third: hold mi until the chord rings. Straight, not squeezed: medium-soft. Headphones on: through a speaker the mic hears the chord too.

measures.en: Your stars are for your third ringing: within 6 cents of pure. The fifth and the root before it were your warm-up.

headline.en: The easiest locks first: the octave, then the fifth. Where the piano puts them is where they ring.

detail.en: The same note, higher: do over a low do
So below over the low do
No shimmer when it's in

text.en: Hold do over the low do: the octave. Straight, not squeezed: medium-soft. Headphones on: through a speaker the mic hears the chord too.
Now so below your note over the same low do: the fifth. Straight, not squeezed: medium-soft. Headphones on: through a speaker the mic hears the chord too.

measures.en: Your stars are for how close your fifth came to ringing: within 6 cents. The octave before it was your warm-up.

headline.en: Start on the piano's third and slide down, slowly, until the chord stops beating. That's the ring: hear it found.

detail.en: Mi, where a piano has it
A hair at a time
The beating stops

text.en: Your hunt: start on mi where the piano has it, slide down slowly until the chord hums, and stay there. Straight, not squeezed: medium-soft. Headphones on: through a speaker the mic hears the chord too.

measures.en: Your stars are for where you stopped: within 6 cents of the ringing third. The result says which way you'd still go.

headline.en: The dominant seventh is the barbershop seventh. Tune it low, lower than you think: 31 cents under the piano's.

detail.en: So, ti, re: the guides
Fa, on top: the seventh
Lower than you think

text.en: Listen to each, as often as you like. Headphones on: through a speaker the mic hears the chord too.

why.en: B's seventh is 31 cents low: it locks. A's is the piano's and shimmers.
A: the low seventh. B is the piano's.
B is only halfway down: still a shimmer. A locks.

text.en: Hold fa on top of so, ti and re, low, until it rings. Straight, not squeezed: medium-soft. Headphones on: through a speaker the mic hears the chord too.

measures.en: Your stars are for your seventh ringing: a barbershop seventh counts close anywhere from 18 cents under the piano's down to pure.

headline.en: Your do is a different pitch in each chord. Hold it where it was and the seventh sounds sharp: let it drop.

detail.en: Do, as the piano has it
Do sharp, the third: 14 cents low
Do as a seventh, 31 cents low; then ti, 14 low

text.en: Through the four chords: do, do sharp, do, ti. Let each one settle where its chord rings. Straight, not squeezed: medium-soft. Headphones on: through a speaker the mic hears the chord too.

measures.en: Your stars are for every held note ringing in its chord, the same do 31 cents lower as the seventh.

headline.en: The hole: the quartet without your part, then with it. The lead sings the tune, the second voice from the top; the others tune to you. On "stream" your note is the chord's seventh: tune it low.

detail.en: Down by the Old Mill Stream (Tell Taylor, 1910)
The others tune around you, except "stream"
The tenor floats above you

text.en: Your part with the guide, at your own pace: "Down by the old mill stream".
Now your part with the other three. Headphones on: through a speaker the mic hears the others too.

measures.en: Your stars are for every note of the tune on pitch, within 20 cents, and "stream" tuned low as the chord's seventh.

headline.en: The hole: the quartet without your part, then with it. The bass is the floor: roots and fifths. Don't push down for depth; keep your chin level.

detail.en: Do, then up a minor third, then so
Never pushed down
No tucking for a low note

text.en: Your part with the guide, at your own pace: "Down by the old mill stream".
Now your part with the other three. Straight, not squeezed: medium-soft. Headphones on: through a speaker the mic hears the others too.

measures.en: Your stars are for your notes on pitch, and for "old" and "stream" ringing in their chords ("mill" is a diminished chord: pitch only).

headline.en: The hole: the quartet without your part, then with it. The tenor floats above the lead, light and soft, lighter than the lead. Bass and lead are the strongest; the tenor the softest.

detail.en: Always over the lead
Softer than you'd think
Bass and lead strong, tenor soft

text.en: Your part with the guide, at your own pace: "Down by the old mill stream".
Now your part with the other three. Straight, not squeezed: medium-soft. Headphones on: through a speaker the mic hears the others too.

measures.en: Your stars are for your notes on pitch, and for "old" and "stream" ringing in their chords ("mill" is a diminished chord: pitch only).

headline.en: The hole: the quartet without your part, then with it. The baritone sings the note the chord still needs, and crosses the lead: above it on the pickup, then under it.

detail.en: What the chord still needs
Above the lead on the pickup, then under
Listen to the chord, not the tune

text.en: Your part with the guide, at your own pace: "Down by the old mill stream".
Now your part with the other three. Straight, not squeezed: medium-soft. Headphones on: through a speaker the mic hears the others too.

measures.en: Your stars are for your notes on pitch, and for "old" and "stream" ringing in their chords ("mill" is a diminished chord: pitch only).

headline.en: A quartet is four seats. First hear which seat is empty; then take the hardest one, the baritone, with no try first.

detail.en: Four rounds
The note the chord still needs
The phrase's held chord

text.en: Each clip is the phrase with one part missing. Which one? Headphones on: through a speaker the mic hears the others too.

why.en: Nothing floats above the tune: the tenor is missing.
No floor under the chords: the bass is missing.
The chord sounds hollow: the baritone, the note it still needs, is missing.
No tune: the lead is missing.

text.en: The baritone with the other three, crossing the lead on the pickup. Straight, not squeezed: medium-soft. Headphones on: through a speaker the mic hears the chord too.

measures.en: Your stars are for your notes on pitch, and for "old" and "stream" ringing in their chords ("mill" is a diminished chord: pitch only).

headline.en: A swipe is one word held while the chords change under it. You're the baritone: your note moves, chord by chord, under the lead's held "Home".

detail.en: "Home", held
Up a third, then down by half steps, and home
The last one, coming home, is the one to aim for

text.en: Try it: your swipe line with the guide, a note at a time: up a third, then down by half steps, on "Home".
Now the swipe for real: each of your notes settling where its chord rings. Straight, not squeezed: medium-soft. Headphones on: through a speaker the mic hears the chord too.

measures.en: Your stars are for each of your notes ringing in its chord (the seventh low, the third low), within 6 cents of pure. The minor chord near the end is judged on pitch.

headline.en: A post is a note held still while the chords move around it. Your note never moves; the chords move around it.

detail.en: The top of the chord
Root, third, fifth, root: your note's job changes
Each breath comes mid-chord; hold through every change

text.en: Hold your note through the four chords, breathing quickly where the screen gives you a gap. Let the chords move; you don't. Straight, not squeezed: medium-soft. Headphones on: through a speaker the mic hears the chord too.

measures.en: Your stars are for your note staying on its pitch while the chords move around it: within 6 cents, every hold.

headline.en: A tag is the end of a song, sung again for the joy of the chord. This one is ours. You'll sing two of its four parts.

detail.en: The tune, on its own over the others
Above your own lead
"Song": make it ring

text.en: Take 1: sing the lead, "Sing just one more song", with the other three around you. Headphones on: through a speaker the mic hears the chord too.
Take 2: the tenor, light and on top, over your own lead. Make "song" ring. Straight, not squeezed: medium-soft. Headphones on: through a speaker the mic hears the chord too.

measures.en: Your stars are for the final chord ringing: your tenor on "song" within 6 cents of pure against the guides, with your own lead playing under you. Two of these four voices are you.
